scenes.headline: How one GPU writes 450 tokens a second
scenes.sub: A hybrid 27B model, a ten-token draft, and a rotated 4-bit cache.
scenes.say: Hi, I'm Toffee! Cinference runs a twenty-seven billion parameter model at four hundred fifty tokens a second, for a single user. Here's how.

scenes.text: The 450 is one forward pass checking ten drafted tokens. With speculation off, the same card does 71.
scenes.say: Four hundred fifty isn't a faster forward pass. It's one pass checking ten drafted tokens at once. With speculation off, the same card does seventy-one.

scenes.title: Tokens per verification round
scenes.say: Each round, a draft head guesses ten tokens, and the full model checks them all in one pass.

parts.note: the draft window: 10 here, up from 5 upstream
parts.say: K is the window: ten, up from five in the upstream engine.
Acceptance is how often the drafts are kept: ninety-three percent at eight K, ninety-eight at two hundred sixty K.
So each round yields ten point three one tokens, rising to ten point eight five.

steps.say: The model's sixty-four layers come in blocks of four. Three are gated DeltaNet, with a fixed-size state that never grows with context.

steps.note: 16 of 64 layers keep a growing cache
steps.say: Only every fourth layer is full attention, sixteen in all, and only those keep a cache that grows with the sequence.
That cache is compressed: rotated by a fixed Hadamard matrix, then keys stored in eight bits, values in four.

scenes.title: Decode tokens per second, by workload
scenes.say: So the speed is a statement about the workload. Recall copies text and accepts nearly every draft. Story writing accepts thirty-seven percent, and lands at one twenty-six.

scenes.text: A speculative throughput is a statement about the workload. Long context holds because 48 of 64 layers keep no growing cache.

recap: One pass verifies ten drafted tokens
Only 16 of 64 layers keep a growing cache
Keys in 8 bits, values in 4, after a rotation
scenes.say: To recap: draft ten, check once, and keep the cache small by design.
